newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed mainly stronger but shorter dated paper dipped amid continuing talk of another rise in Dutch official interest rates.
The guilder also continued to lose ground against the mark, fuelling speculation that the Dutch central bank will hike the special advances rate to support the Dutch unit.
Some dealers said they expected a 10 basis point increase in this key rate to 3.10 percent, 10 basis points above German's equivalent, the repo rate, perhaps as early as Thursday.
"But I think the market is a bit mixed about that," said one dealer.
The mark has risen strongly against the guilder, passing the central parity rate under the European exchange rate mechanism of 1.12673 guilders and hitting 1.1269 today.
Some analysts have attributed this trend to switching by investors out of Dutch bonds into Bunds, which are trading at yield premium to guilder paper despite recent convergence.
Dutch money market rates and short bond yields have risen in recent weeks on expectations of a rate hike, contributing to a marked flattening of the guilder yield curve.
But traders said the curve and Dutch-German yield spreads were relatively steady today in quiet trading.
Dealers said selling by domestic Dutch investors of 2001 paper highlighted otherwise listless trading.
One dealer noted that the 8.50 percent March 2001 bond came under pressure.
The Dutch market achieved most of its gains on the opening, following Bunds which responded to a firmer close by U.S. Treasuries.

U.S. second-quarter employment cost data issued midway through the afternoon was in line with expectations, leaving market players to look forward to July non-payrolls figures on Friday for signs of where the U.S. market is heading.
